implementation_statement: No access policy existed before this work. POL-02 (P06), which also holds the program governance rules and staff use rules, was approved 2026-08-31 and takes effect 2026-09-01. A one-page joiner and leaver checklist is due 2026-09-30.

The Owner, Shop Manager, and 3 technicians have named SYS-01 accounts. The MSP creates productivity suite accounts on the Shop Manager's request. Gaps: both Counter Associates use one shared SYS-01 'Counter' login whose password has not changed since 2024, although a Counter Associate who knew it left on 2026-05-08; no account review; no leaver checklist.
evidence: SYS-01 user list; productivity suite user export; staff roster

implementation_statement: SYS-01 enforces three roles (administrator, technician, counter). Gap: the ticket note field, where passcodes and account passwords are typed, is visible to every role, and the platform offers a restricted field that is not used.

Counter Associates cannot export reports. Gaps: all 3 technicians hold the SYS-01 'manager' role, which allows full customer exports; the bench PCs run under one shared local administrator account; no rule limits what technicians may open on a customer device.
evidence: SYS-01 role list; bench PC account list

implementation_statement: Both SaaS services lock accounts after repeated failed sign-ins using vendor defaults (confirmed in settings on 2026-07-22).
evidence: SYS-01 and productivity suite security settings

implementation_statement: The MSP enforces a 10-minute screen lock on the 4 office endpoints. Gap: the bench PCs never lock, and the counter PCs stay signed in to SYS-01 all day under the shared login.

Staff reach SaaS systems over the internet with MFA on named accounts; there is no VPN. The MSP reaches office endpoints through its remote management tool. Gap: no evidence that the MSP tool requires MFA or which MSP technicians have access. The Senior Technician installed a free remote desktop tool on one bench PC to help customers remotely.
evidence: MSP remote tool description; bench PC software list

implementation_statement: Staff Wi-Fi uses WPA2 with a shared password; guest Wi-Fi is separated with internet access only. Gap: customer devices under repair join the staff Wi-Fi, which also carries the counter PCs, bench PCs, and bench storage.

Gap: new staff get an informal walkthrough only; no security, privacy, phishing, or payment terminal training. Planned: 30-minute training at hire and every year, quarterly phishing simulations, and terminal tamper training from 2026-10.

provider_if_inherited: Ticketing and POS vendor; productivity suite vendor
implementation_statement: SYS-01 records sign-ins, ticket views, and exports by user (but the shared Counter login hides who acted). The productivity suite records sign-ins with default settings. Gap: nothing is logged on the bench PCs or bench storage.
evidence: SYS-01 audit log sample; suite audit settings

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Gap: nobody reviews the SYS-01 audit log or suite sign-in alerts. Planned: a monthly 20-minute review of SYS-01 exports, bulk ticket views, and after-hours sign-ins, and suite sign-in alerts, starting 2026-10, recorded on a checklist.

provider_if_inherited: Ticketing and POS vendor; productivity suite vendor
implementation_statement: SYS-01 keeps its audit log for 12 months (vendor documentation). Gap: the productivity suite keeps audit logs only for its plan's default period, shorter than one year.
The first independent control assessment ran 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-12 (P07). Gap: no commitment to repeat it each year until POL-02 A.6 took effect.

Gap: bench PCs run any diagnostic or flashing tool from any source, including forum downloads, and allow USB storage. Planned: an approved bench tool list and USB storage blocked except on the data transfer station by 2026-11-30.
Gap: no inventory of devices, SaaS services, or where customer data is kept, and no list of payment terminals with serial numbers. Planned: a one-page inventory and a terminal list by 2026-10-31.
Gap: no contingency plan. The BIA (P05) was approved 2026-08-31. Planned: a short contingency plan with paper downtime steps and a hurricane checklist by 2026-11-30.
Gap: no plan test and no restore test of the cloud backup has ever been run. Planned: first restore test by 2026-09-30, then quarterly, and a tabletop exercise by 2026-11-30.

SYS-01 data is backed up by its vendor. The MSP backs up the productivity suite and the bench storage nightly to SYS-08 with 1-year retention. Gaps: backups are not immutable; one MSP administrator login can delete them; customer data is kept in the backup for a year after the job ends.

provider_if_inherited: Ticketing and POS vendor; productivity suite vendor
implementation_statement: Named accounts for 5 of 7 staff in SYS-01 and for all staff in the suite. Gap: the shared Counter login and the shared bench account do not identify the person.

MFA is on for the SYS-01 administrator accounts and the merchant portal. Gap: the cloud backup console and the firewall management login, both held by the MSP, accept a password alone; the bench storage administrator account has no MFA.
SaaS services enforce minimum password length. Gaps: the Counter password is unchanged since 2024; the bench storage administrator password is written on a label on the device (found 2026-08-11).
Gap: incidents are handled ad hoc (the 2026-03-14 photo complaint had no written record). Planned: POL-03 and the P08 runbook, approved 2026-08-31; tabletop by 2026-11-30.
Gap: no reporting rule; staff do not know whom to tell or the processor's notice term. Planned: report to the Shop Manager within 1 hour (POL-03 4.2) from 2026-09-01.
Gap: no incident response plan before 2026-08-31. Planned: the P08 runbook, with a printed binder at the counter, tested by 2026-11-30.
The back room has a keypad lock. Gap: customer drives awaiting the outside lab and recovery drives sit in an open bin on the bench; the keypad code has not changed since 2023.

Gap: recycling drop-off devices and retired shop PCs get a factory reset only, with no record per device and no check. Planned: a sanitization standard based on NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 (Clear, Purge, or Destroy by media type; cryptographic erase for encrypted phones; verification; a record per device) by 2026-10-31.
evidence: Recycler pickup certificates (per pickup, not per device)

implementation_statement: Gap: USB storage is allowed on all bench PCs and technicians sometimes use their own drives for transfers. Planned: company-issued encrypted drives only, on the data transfer station only, by 2026-11-30.
Keyed storefront, keypad on the back room, after-hours alarm, cameras at the counter and bench, locked parts cabinet and recycling cage. Gap: the keypad code is shared and unchanged since 2023.
This SSP was approved by the Owner on 2026-08-31.
Gap: no written staff rules. Planned: POL-02 Part C acknowledgments signed by all 7 staff by 2026-09-30.
The Owner designated the Shop Manager as Security and Privacy Lead in writing on 2026-07-15.
The 2 technicians hired in 2025 had background checks through a screening vendor. Gap: staff hired earlier were not checked, and there is no rule for which roles need a check.
Gap: leavers are handled informally; the shared Counter password was not changed when a Counter Associate left on 2026-05-08. Planned: same-day leaver checklist from 2026-09-30.
Gap: no confidentiality agreement covers customer device data. Planned: a signed customer data confidentiality agreement for all 7 staff by 2026-09-30.
Gap: no sanctions rule. Planned: POL-02 A.4 from 2026-09-01.
The first risk assessment was completed 2026-07-31 with NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01); an update is due every July.
Gap: no vulnerability scanning of the shop network or endpoints. Planned: quarterly internal scan by the MSP from 2026-12.

The merchant agreement and the SYS-01, suite, and MSP contracts are on file. Gaps: no vendor list; the outside data recovery lab, the courier, the recycler, and the AI assistant's model provider have no security or data-use terms; the MSP contract has no incident notice term.
The MSP firewall blocks unsolicited inbound traffic and separates guest Wi-Fi. Gap: inside the shop one flat network carries counter PCs, bench PCs, bench storage, and customer devices under repair.

implementation_statement: The 2 laptops are encrypted by the MSP. Gaps: the 2 counter PCs, the bench PCs, and the bench storage are not encrypted; customer passcodes sit in clear text in SYS-01 ticket notes.
The MSP patches the 4 office endpoints and the firewall monthly. Gap: the bench PCs and bench storage are outside the MSP contract and are patched only when the Senior Technician remembers.
MSP antivirus runs on the 4 office endpoints. Gap: built-in antivirus on the bench PCs is often turned off because flashing tools trigger it; nobody watches alerts after hours.
Gap: no monitoring beyond antivirus. Planned: MSP-managed EDR with alert monitoring on office and bench PCs and SYS-01 export alerts by 2026-12-31.

Gap: no retention rule. Customer data stays on the bench storage indefinitely (about 2.3 TB from about 610 jobs older than 30 days) and in the backup for a year; passcodes stay in ticket notes forever. Planned: POL-04 retention rules from 2026-09-01; backlog purge by 2026-11-30.
